subject: humanities
passage: In the humid climate of southern India, the palm-leaf manuscripts on which Tamil literature was long preserved seldom last more than a few centuries, so a text survived only if it was copied again and again. As a result, the oldest surviving manuscript of a work is often far younger than the work itself. Consider a Tamil devotional poem whose oldest known manuscript was copied in the 1700s. Literary historian Kavitha Raman has shown that a commentary on Tamil grammar, written by a scholar whose life can be dated to the 1200s by temple inscriptions, quotes several passages from the poem as examples of fine style. Raman's evidence indicates that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: at least the quoted passages of the poem already existed by the 1200s, centuries before 1700.
choices.B: the grammar scholar wrote the poem himself and then claimed that an earlier poet had written it.
choices.C: every Tamil poem quoted by medieval scholars survives in some manuscript older than the 1700s.
choices.D: the poem was most likely composed in the 1700s, when its oldest known manuscript was copied.

explanation.why: Palm-leaf copies rarely last long, so a manuscript from the 1700s says little about when the poem was written. A scholar from the 1200s quoted passages from it, and he could only quote lines that already existed. The quoted passages therefore date to the 1200s or earlier.
explanation.A: Correct. A writer of the 1200s could quote only passages that existed in his time, so the quoted lines are at least that old.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text gives no reason to think the scholar wrote the poem.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This poem's oldest manuscript is from the 1700s, which contradicts the claim.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text explains that the oldest manuscript is often much younger than the work, and the quotations show the poem is older than 1700.
